evidence.detail: FR-PROXY-014 Requirement (22.reverse-proxy.srs.md:1162): 'passing for HEAD and 304 the `Content-Length` value when it is a single all-digit value or several identical ones and `-1` otherwise'. The value `Content-Length: 99999999999999999999` is a single all-digit value, so the statement requires passing it, but it exceeds Long.MAX_VALUE 9223372036854775807 and cannot be the `long contentLength` argument of `res.relay(in, contentLength)` (FR-HTTP-037). The request-side parser it is meant to mirror bounds the same input: SEC-PROXY-003 Requirement 'Content-Length elements required to be digits that fit in a long and compared numerically' and SEC-PROXY-003 AC-2 'Content-Length: 99999999999999999999 ... get 400'. Secondary: 'several identical ones' vs SEC-PROXY-004 AC-7 'Content-Length: 5 and Content-Length: 05 are read as 5-byte bodies' (numeric equality) leaves undecided whether HEAD/304 lines `10` and `010` give 10 or -1.

findings.description: The bodyless lenient Content-Length rule (round-2 statement and AC-6) prescribes an impossible action for an all-digit value that overflows long and does not say whether identity is textual or numeric; an implementer must guess (NumberFormatException -> -1?).
